items.rootCause:
I could not name the exact exception: it never happens in Jest, and I had no device or logcat. What I could establish:

(1) THE MECHANISM, read in the shipped code; it explains every symptom. When an exception is not caught, React Native calls ReactHostImpl.handleHostException. ExpoReactHostFactory.handleInstanceException passes it to expo-updates. ErrorRecovery.onReactInstanceException ignores it once 10 s have passed since content appeared, and nothing rethrows. Then ReactHostImpl.destroy() empties the surface. What is left is the window background, colors.xml activityBackground #0f1218 = color.bg. That matches the report exactly:
- every pixel is (15,18,24), with no ambient digits;
- uiautomator sees only the root views, so even the 'ambient' id is gone;
- Back leaves the app, because with no instance onBackPressed returns false and the activity's default runs;
- relaunching gives a new instance, which opens Home;
- the search's websocket dies with the JS runtime, so no game is counted.
A render error would show ErrorScreen through the root ErrorBoundary instead. So the cause is either a JS fatal outside React (a timer, a native callback, a Reanimated worklet error reported to JS as fatal) or a non-ignorable exception while Fabric mounts: MountItemDispatcher rethrows it, and GuardedFrameCallback hands it to reactContext.handleException. A debug build would show a red box. Moshe's black screens of 1.0.0 were probably the same mechanism.

(2) IT IS A REGRESSION FROM TONIGHT. QA run #2, item postgame-results-v2-new-game-ranked, passed on 02.11 at 10:06 on the 01.11 01:12 build: it was tapped twice, a stealth bot came in about 2 s, and the cancel worked. No source file changed between 01.11 01:12 and af4c8a (03.11 00:43). Both of tonight's builds fail 3 out of 3. So the cause is in round 1 (00:43–04:36). The 09:07-only changes are ruled out: Enter in its fix2 form, and the perf round's afterFrames, CSS Spinner and ResultsLoading, which are newer than both builds.
- Round-1 files on this path: tactile/Button/slant (the results action pair, FoundView's VS), AvatarArt plus the new SvgMarkup (a cached SVG tree, which Jest mocks), useScreenFocused/HomeScreen, MatchScreen/matchModel, the OnlineSession profiles getter, ResultsScreen (CountChips, MoveText, header), Avatar, Rating and Badges.
- The server change (FOUND_HOLD_MS) adds no message types.

(3) THE JS FLOW IS FINE. I reproduced the whole flow in Jest through the real routes: ranked game → results → 'משחק חדש' → leave() → startRankedAndOpen('replace') → searching → found (a rematch) → 3-2-1 → board. It ran with Hermes' missing globals removed and Reduced Motion off. It stays on /match: the old session is let go, a new search runs in the same queue, and there is no fallback, no ErrorScreen and nothing reported. So the cause is in what Jest stubs: react-native-screens' native replace, Reanimated's UI thread and layout animations, react-native-svg drawing (SvgAst), and the Colyseus/Firebase SDKs.

(4) WHAT IS UNIQUE TO THIS PATH:
- 'משחק חדש' is the only way off Results by replace. In one transaction, Results and its just-pressed, still-springing tactile button are removed, and a new screen full of SVG is inserted into the native stack.
- The ways that work are pop ('לבית'), push (Home's 'עוד סיבוב'), and the game→results and match→game replaces.
- Results is also the only screen in the app that uses Reanimated layout animations (entering=).
- The recordings show the screen frozen for 0.8–1.2 s before going dark. That fits a stalled UI thread (the 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed' flood described in docs/PERF.md) ending in the fatal exception.

(5) PRACTICE AND FRIENDS take the same path: startAndOpen(...,'replace') to /game, and router.replace to /friends/room or /friends/join. They are exposed to the same class of bug and were not tried on tonight's builds.

items.rootCause: The server timing is right: it sends `found` at F, holds 1.2 s, then sends `countdown` with startsAt = now + 3000. The client side has the problem. At F + 1.2 s + latency, MatchScreen swapped FoundView for CountdownView in a single commit. That one frame deleted views the VS had just animated (its enter and slam springs, the avatars' nod layers) and also drew the count's two new SVG avatars (about 200 shapes) for the first time. That is the case docs/PERF.md B14/B32 describes: Reanimated fails once per new shape for every just-moved view deleted in that frame. Add the React render of the two avatars, and the count's first frame reached the screen 0.45 s late with reduced motion on, and 1.0–1.5 s late with it off (it is off on phone 3). Meanwhile the count was anchored to its render time (countdownSince) and the JS ticks kept running, so the model had already moved to '2'. The first frame that was drawn was also at opacity ~0 (useEnter): a blank frame, then '2'. The recordings show that the JS thought the count started on time: in rec b1/g3/p1-g3, '2' and '1' each last ~0.95 s and GO falls on the 1-second grid, so the even spread (countdownStepOver) never started; it only reacts to a late render, not a late draw. The VS staying past its time is the same stall: the old frame stays on screen (in RF8Y30L038L-g3 frames 13600–14850 are byte-identical). GO lasting 1.3–1.5 s = 400 ms counted from GO's first render, plus a tick, plus the game screen's mount and flow.fade. On the A16 those last two take ~1 s (GO 15250 → board 16700 in rec b1). More server lead cannot shorten GO, because the board needs the snapshot and the server sends it only at GO; and once the switch draws little, the count needs no extra lead.
items.fix:
Client only, no server timeline change.
(1) MatchScreen draws the VS and the count as one stage of two absolute layers that cross-fade (240 ms; reduced motion 200 ms). Once the count starts, the VS stays mounted under it, hidden, still and a11y-hidden, until the screen goes; a memo stops it re-rendering. So nothing just-moved is deleted in the frame that draws new SVG.
(2) Behind the VS, the count gets ready unseen once FoundView reports onSettled (its badges popped and drawn, or the VS drawn with reduced motion). Its two avatars' React work happens during the VS. CountdownView got `revealed`: while false there is no digit and no announcement, so each digit still slams in when it is seen.
(3) The count is anchored to its first drawn frame. useDrawnAt = afterFrames(SWAP_FRAMES) after the commit. matchModel.countdownShownAt keeps the render time if the frame came within COUNTDOWN_DRAW_SLACK_MS (150), so the server's whole seconds stay. If the frame came later, the count runs evenly from that frame. Before it is drawn, the first digit holds. The countdown beat sound also waits for that first frame.
(4) GO: the game opens goHoldMs(reduce) = 400 − flow fade = 160 ms after GO! is first drawn (200 ms with reduced motion). It used to be 400 ms after GO's first render. The game screen's own fade over GO! makes up the 400 ms, and a slow phone keeps GO! on screen while it draws, with nothing added on top.
Docs: motion.md rows vs.slam, countdown.digit and go; 01-SPEC §10 (ספירה לאחור).

Install the NEW APK (this tree) on BOTH phones. In the last check they ran different APKs: phone 1 had the 09:07 build, phone 3 the 04:37 build. Staging needs no deploy for this.
Ranked 2p מהיר, both phones searching at once. Record both with `screenrecord --size 540x1170` and extract frames every 50 ms (rec/thumbs.ps1). Do 3 runs with reduced motion off, then 2 with it on, then 1 against the ranked bot.
What must be seen:
(a) 'נמצא יריב!' stays about 1.2–1.4 s from its first frame. It cross-fades into the count over ~240 ms, with no dark frame between.
(b) '3' is the first digit in every run. '3', '2' and '1' each last 0.85–1.05 s. If a phone still stalls, the three are equal and shorter, never '2' first or '2' for 0.3 s.
(c) The beat sound and haptic come with each visible digit.

Optional root-cause check: run `adb logcat -c` before the match, then after GO run `adb logcat -d | grep -c 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed'`. Around the VS→count switch it should now be close to 0.

items.rootCause: FoundView popped the badges with setTimeout(800) from its own JS mount. The server starts the count 1200 ms after `found`, and the count unmounted FoundView. On phone 3, the VS's JS render (two new SVG avatars, about 300 ms of React work per docs/PERF.md, more on a busy phone) came about 0.5–0.6 s after `found`. In rec RF8Y30L038L-g3 the search screen keeps animating until 12800 and the VS's first frame is at 12900; the 1-second grid puts the count's JS start at about 13400. So the pop was due at about found + 1.3–1.4 s, after the count had already replaced the VS. The screen then froze on the badge-less VS until 14850 (the switch stall of M1). On Android, JS timers also fire only on UI-thread frames, so any stall delays them further. The reaction had a similar cause: useReadyFace nods only when `ready` flips after mount, and the nod's layer stack was deleted mid-way by the count switch. In frames 13050–13300 the avatar regions do not change at all.
items.fix:
(1) FoundView takes `badgesAt` (absolute, clock time). MatchScreen passes the first render of this match's `found` + metrics.vs.badgesAtMs (800). The pop no longer depends on how late the VS mounted, and has at least 400 ms before the count.
(2) FoundView takes `active`: once the count shows, the VS is kept hidden under it instead of being unmounted (M1). Nothing pops while hidden.
(3) SeatTile: the nod is now tied to the readiness shown on screen, useReadyFace(showReady && seat.ready). Every ready player nods once, when their 'מוכן' badge pops, even if they were in before the VS was first drawn. A player who connects after the pop nods when they get in. The smile mood still follows seat.ready. With reduced motion the badges are there at once and only the face changes, as before.
Docs: motion.md vs.slam row, 01-SPEC §10.
items.test: MatchScreen.test.tsx: 'the "מוכן" badges pop 800 ms after "found", not after the VS mounted: a VS drawn late still shows them (QA B43)'. The layers move after showReady flips, then one still picture. I confirmed both fail with the old logic: an 800 ms mount-relative timer, and useReadyFace(seat.ready).
items.deviceCheck: Phone 3 (RF8Y30L038L), reduced motion OFF, and phone 1 as well, 3 ranked 2p games, recorded at 50 ms frames. On 'נמצא יריב!' the 'מוכן' badges must appear on both tiles about 0.8 s after the search screen left: 0.1–0.6 s after the VS's first frame, depending on how late the VS drew. They must stay at least 0.4 s before the count. Each avatar must nod as its badge appears: about 0.9 s of movement in the avatar area, smile kept. Then the cross-fade into '3'. With reduced motion ON, the badges are there with the VS and there is no nod movement.

items.rootCause: This was a measurement artifact, not an early timeout. Timestamps in the phone agent's transcript (wf_84f2ae51-806, agent a5f23e…): the screenrecord+tap command started at 08:42:32.3 (the tap about 1 s later, the search clock at 0:00 about 2.4 s into the video). After `sleep 17.5` it ran `adb.ts ui`. uiautomator cannot get an idle state while the search radar animates, and adb.ts retries for up to ~30 s. That call returned only at 08:43:30.3 with no output. The next dump, the one that showed match-timeout '1:00', finished at 08:43:40.6, about 65 s after the search started. The video itself is only 18.9 s long (--time-limit 19), so the '~20 s' was the agent's estimate. Code: every queue size times out only when now ≥ ticket.deadline = searchStart + MATCH_TIMEOUT_MS (60 s) in matcher.matchTick. The client shows the server's elapsedMs ('1:00'), and the search clock (0:16 at 18.5 s) matched the server's time. Spec §10: '3–4 שחקנים… ממתין עד 60 שניות'. The text 'חיפשנו דקה שלמה' matches the real wait.

fix:match.notes:
- Server: no code change, so no deploy is needed. The only server file touched is a guard test. I kept the server timeline (found → 1.2 s hold → countdown, GO at countdown start + 3 s), for these reasons. GO's length on the A16 is set by the game screen's mount after the snapshot, and the server sends the snapshot only at GO, so more lead cannot hide that mount. The '3' loss came from the client's single-commit switch; that switch now draws little. A lead would also make old builds show '3' for longer.
- Decision I made on my own, flagged for Moshe: on the VS, in full motion, each avatar now nods when its 'מוכן' badge pops. Before, a player who was in before the VS was first drawn never nodded, and one who turned ready before the pop nodded right away. The smile mood is unchanged, and so is reduced motion. The GO hold is now 160 ms from GO!'s first drawn frame plus the game screen's 240 ms flow.fade (reduced motion: 200 + 200), instead of 400 ms from GO's first render. motion.md and 01-SPEC §10 are updated to match.
- Residual for M1: on the A16, GO! will still last about 1.0–1.25 s, because the game screen takes ~1 s to mount and draw (the perf round's route warm-up and game-hitch items). The single blank frame before GO! is GO's slam starting at opacity 0 (by design, one frame). The dim frame before the board is the game screen's flow.fade.
- Possible follow-up, out of scope: search → VS still deletes the SearchView (radar, my avatar's stage layers) in the frame that first draws the VS's avatars. That is the same B14/B32 rule, and it is why the VS appears a little late on phone 3. M2's absolute badge time covers it.
- The fix check used two different APKs (phone 1: 09:07, phone 3: 04:37). Install one build on both before the device check.
- Peer files untouched. No git, adb or build. Formatting was applied by hand, only to my own lines. Temporary copies made to confirm the new tests fail on the old logic are in the scratchpad (matchModel.mine.ts, parts.mine.tsx, FoundView.mine.tsx); the real files were restored and verified. issues.problem: The recordings narrow the failure further than the report says, and the device check should be sharpened to match. The failure is in the native mount of the replace commit (UI thread), not a later JS timer. Two of the report's own pieces of evidence point there.
issues.evidence:
rec/RF8Y30L038L-n1c frames 00000–00800 are the unchanged Results screen ('משחק חדש' still showing). Frame 00900 onward is solid (15,18,24), and no frame of /match is ever drawn. The ambient layer is Skia, drawn from a Reanimated useFrameCallback on the UI thread (components/ambient/AmbientCanvas.tsx), so identical frames mean the UI thread stopped producing frames. A JS-thread fatal alone would leave the digits moving until the host is destroyed.

I checked in node_modules that the flood the report suggests is not fatal by itself:
- Reanimated 4.5.1 NativeProxy.synchronouslyUpdateUIProps catches and only logs with Log.w ('synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed for tag').
- RN 0.86 SynchronousMountItem.execute catches too.

The report's teardown mechanism checks out: ReactHostImpl.handleHostException → ExpoReactHostFactory.handleInstanceException, which does not rethrow while handlers exist → expo-updates ErrorRecovery, which stops handling 10 s after CONTENT_APPEARED → destroy(). So something else throws during the same stalled mount.
issues.suggestion:
Add to the logcat grep:
- 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed' (count it)
- 'Skipped .* frames'
- 'dispatchMountItems'
- 'Unable to find viewState'
- 'RetryableMountingLayerException'
- 'IllegalViewOperationException'
- 'specified child already has a parent'

issues.evidence:

Inside it, each slanted Button now adds Slant views: collapsable={false}, rotate+scale transforms, edge and plate (tactile.tsx, slant.tsx, 00:56–00:57, before the 04:36 build).

review:black.summary:
Verdict: the critical item is not fixed. The agent changed no production code and returned 'needs-moshe'. The diagnosis is honest and mostly checks out, but the black screen still happens on the current tree.

Confirmed:
- The regression is real and new tonight. In QA run #2 (run2.json), postgame-results-v2-new-game-ranked passed on 02.11 at 10:06 on the build from before tonight. Both of tonight's builds went black 3 out of 3 times.
- The silent-black mechanism holds in node_modules. In release, ReactHostImpl.handleHostException goes to ExpoReactHostFactory, which does not rethrow while handlers exist. expo-updates ErrorRecovery stops handling 10 s after content appears. Then the host is destroyed, leaving only the window background #0f1218.
- The Reanimated 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps' flood and SynchronousMountItem both catch their errors, so the stall alone is not fatal.
- The recording (rec/RF8Y30L038L-n1c) shows the Results screen frozen until about 0.9 s, then solid black, and no /match frame is ever drawn. The ambient layer is Skia on the UI thread and is frozen too. This points to a failure while the replace commit mounts (Results deleted and the new SVG screen added in one commit), not to a later JS timer.

Not covered by the report: tonight's new views inside the deleted Results subtree (Slant on the action pair inside the only entering= views in the app, and AvatarArt's retired stacks kept 4 s). The 5 s A/B wait should be 6 s or more. I checked the brief's Enter lead: the match views use their own useEnter (unchanged), not ui/Enter, so it does not apply.

Checks I ran:
- The new test passes (52 s suite), but it is coverage only and does not reproduce the bug.
- tsc -p apps/mobile is clean.
- eslint and prettier --check on the test file are clean.

issues.problem: The VS kept under the count is not still, though the report says it is. The M2 change starts a nod in each VS avatar when its 'מוכן' badge pops (found+800 ms). AvatarArt's own timers end that nod 900 ms later, and the memo on FoundView does not stop them. So during the count (usually during '3'; during '2' on a slow phone; 3–4 avatars at a 3–4 table) the hidden VS re-renders each avatar from its layer stack to a new StaticArt. That costs React work per shape plus a first SVG draw inside the alpha-0 layer, and the retired layers are deleted 4 s later. M1 assumes nothing new is drawn once the count runs. This is new SVG work during the count, and this round introduced it: before, the VS was deleted at the switch. If that commit lands in the same UI frame as a digit change, the frame also deletes the old Step (key change), whose ring and slam a worklet moved within the last 2 s. That gives the B14/B32 failures (shapes × deleted views, about 1 ms each), the same stall the round set out to remove. Even without that, 100–300 ms of JS on the A16 (more with 4 avatars) can hold the 100 ms tick past a digit boundary and make the digits uneven.
issues.evidence: apps/mobile/src/screens/match/parts.tsx: `useReadyFace(showReady && seat.ready)`, so the nod starts when the badges pop. apps/mobile/src/avatars/AvatarArt.tsx useReaction: `at(total, () => mine(() => null))` ends the reaction from AvatarArt's own timer, then renders `<StaticArt key={STILL_KEY} …>`, a new mount of the picture, while useRetiredStacks keeps the layers for 4 s. packages/avatars/src/motion.ts: nod durationMs 900. The repo's own matchFaces.test.tsx (new B43 case) shows the picture going from >1 SvgXml back to 1 after the nod. MatchScreen.tsx says 'still and unseen … a memo stops it re-rendering'. Its test 'the VS stays under the count, unseen and still' checks only that the instance is the same, plus opacity and pointerEvents, not that nothing redraws. Rough timeline on a fast phone: pop F+0.8, nod ends about F+1.7, count shown about F+1.25, '2' about F+2.25. On phone 3: reveal about F+1.5–1.6, nod-end render about F+1.8–2.1, '2' about F+2.4.
issues.suggestion: Freeze the VS avatars once `active` is false. A nod that is still running when the count takes over must not swap back to a new StaticArt under the count. For example, keep the current stack still (as AvatarArt's covered-stage path does), or end the nod without remounting the picture. Alternatively, time the nod so it ends before the count can start. Avoid simply passing reaction=null: that path also remounts StaticArt. Add a regression test: after the count starts, advance 2 s and assert that the hidden VS avatars' SvgXml set/picture does not change (no new StaticArt mount).

issues.problem: goHoldMs subtracts the iOS `flow.fade` (240 ms; reduced 200 ms) from the 400 ms GO hold. On Android, react-native-screens' 'fade' is fixed at 150 ms and ignores animationDuration. The new motion.md/01-SPEC text '160 ms + the game screen's 240 ms fade makes up 400 ms' is therefore wrong on Android. 01-SPEC §10 also still says GO! stays at least 400 ms before the board replaces it. On a quick Android phone, the board is fully in about 160 + 150 ms after GO! is drawn, plus the game screen's own mount.
issues.evidence: node_modules/react-native-screens/android/src/main/res/base/anim/rns_fade_in.xml: android:duration="150". FragmentTransactionKt.kt maps FADE to rns_fade_in/rns_fade_out. apps/mobile/src/theme/transitions.ts: '(The durations are iOS's; Android fades at its own pace.)'. MatchScreen.tsx goHoldMs: `GO_HOLD_MS - (reduce ? motion.duration.reducedFade : motion.duration.stateChange)`.
issues.suggestion: Either make the hold Platform-aware (Android: 400 − 150), or keep 160 ms and correct motion.md `go` and 01-SPEC §10 so they say what Android really does. On slow phones the game-screen mount hides the difference, but the docs should not claim 400 ms.

issues.problem: M1 is still partial, as reported. On the A16, GO! will last about 1.0–1.25 s instead of the required ~0.4 s, because the game screen's mount after the snapshot (perf round) still dominates. Also, the core device premise is checked only by code reading, not on a device: (a) Android records and draws the SVG of the alpha-0 'prepared' count during the VS; (b) two rAFs (bridgeless rAF = setTimeout(0), fired on Choreographer TIMERS_EVENTS after DISPATCH_UI) come after the frame is drawn. Both look sound from the code. In the rare case where a commit reaches the UI thread between DISPATCH_UI and TIMERS of a frame, the second rAF fires before that frame's draw, so a long draw would be underestimated.
issues.evidence: ReactCommon/react/runtime/TimerManager.cpp: 'The current implementation of requestAnimationFrame is the same as setTimeout(0)'. JavaTimerManager.kt fires timers in TimerFrameCallback on ReactChoreographer TIMERS_EVENTS. The Jest tests mock afterFrames, so they prove the model's logic but not the timing on the phone.
issues.suggestion: Keep the device check the report gives: same APK on both phones; screenrecord at 50 ms frames; 3 runs with reduced motion off, 2 with it on, 1 against the bot. Also run `adb logcat -c` before and count `synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed` after. Additionally look at the '3'→'2' boundary for a stall, and at a 3–4 player VS→count (issue 1). Escalate the GO length to the perf round (game-screen warm-up).

review:match.summary:
Verdict: issues. The approach is sound, but its premise has one gap and a few smaller points remain.

Checks I ran, all green:
- screens/match: 6 suites, 72 tests.
- ranked.e2e, rankedNewGame.e2e, roomLinks.e2e and server matchmaking/service.test.ts: 82 tests.
- interferenceRanked.e2e and a11yAudit: 162 tests.
- `tsc -p apps/mobile` is clean, and `eslint --max-warnings 0` passes on the 5 changed source files.

**M1 (partial, as reported)**
The diagnosis holds against the code and docs/PERF.md. A deleted view fails only in the frame it is deleted, before reportMount. The old switch to the count deleted the VS's just-moved views in the frame that drew the count's avatars for the first time.
- The new stage keeps the VS mounted under the count, so the switch deletes nothing.
- The count is built behind the VS once the badges are out. Android still records a view at alpha 0, so its first SVG draw moves into the VS time.
- The count is anchored to its first drawn frame (useDrawnAt with two rAFs). In bridgeless RN 0.86, rAF is setTimeout(0), fired on the Choreographer's TIMERS step, which runs after the frame's mount step.
- countdownShownAt holds '3' until that first frame, then spreads 3·2·1 evenly. Against the server clock offset and the stale useNow value it holds up.
- Practice, friends and levels are unaffected: FriendsCountdown is separate, and SeatTile, FoundView and CountdownView are used only by the ranked MatchScreen.

Gaps in M1:
- **Medium:** the hidden VS is not still. The new nod at the badge pop ends 900 ms later through AvatarArt's own timers, which the memo does not stop. Each VS avatar then gets a new still picture: JS work and a first SVG draw, under the count. Landing on a digit change, this can uneven the digits or bring back B14/B32 failures. No test covers it.
- **Low:** goHoldMs assumes the 240 ms fade, which is iOS's. react-native-screens on Android fades in 150 ms, so the docs' "160 + 240 = 400" is wrong there.
- **Low:** GO! will still last ~1.0–1.25 s on the A16 (the game screen's mount). The phone-side timing has only been checked from the code.

**M2 (fixed)**
badgesAt is absolute (found + 800 ms), so a late-drawn VS still shows the badges; the test is correct. In full motion the nod is now tied to the badge, which is what brings in M1's medium issue.

**M3 (cannot-reproduce, conclusion confirmed)**
- The phone agent's transcript shows the tap at 08:42:32 and the dump that showed match-timeout '1:00' at 08:43:40, about 67 s later.
- The video is 18.90 s long and its last frame shows 0:16 still searching.
- On the server, every search times out at searchStart + MATCH_TIMEOUT_MS (60 s), with no environment override. On the client, the timeout comes only from the server's message.
